iron_arrow.name: iron arrow
iron_arrow.lore: Many a battlefield has been strewn with these simple shafts of ash-wood and their heads of hammered iron. They are cheaply made and can be trusted well enough in the hunt, and in their time they have brought down game and men beyond counting.

steel_arrow.name: steel arrow
steel_arrow.lore: Fletchers bind these points of tempered steel to straight-grained shafts of cedar with silken thread. The points hold their edge through stone and bone alike, and they pass with ease through light armour.

hardened_gold_arrow.name: hardened gold arrow
hardened_gold_arrow.lore: By the art of the alchemists gold may be hardened to serve for an arrowhead, and it strikes more heavily than iron or steel. Archers prize such arrows, and in their flight they shine like tiny suns.

diamond_arrow.name: diamond arrow
diamond_arrow.lore: Ground finer than any edge of steel, these points of diamond strike more heavily than gold. None but the wealthiest archers can afford to loose such arrows and afterward to leave them lying where they fell.

dragonbone_arrow.name: dragonbone arrow
dragonbone_arrow.lore: In the hollow bones of ancient dragons there lingers a whisper of the dragon's nature, and from such bones these shafts are carved. They strike with the weight of legend, and few wounds go deeper than theirs.

iron_bolt.name: iron bolt
iron_bolt.lore: Short and stout are these bolts of iron that are made for the crossbow, and what they lose in range they gain in force. Those who fight in dungeons favour them, since a charging foe must often be halted there with little time to spare.

steel_bolt.name: steel bolt
steel_bolt.lore: These bolts of steel, ground with great care and fletched as quarrels are, fly steadily in close quarters. Their hardened heads flatten when they strike and so tear a wide wound, for which reason they are cruellest against a foe who goes without armour.

hardened_gold_bolt.name: hardened gold bolt
hardened_gold_bolt.lore: The gold of these gleaming bolts was hardened by the art of the alchemists. They strike more heavily than steel, and for this the hunters of monsters prize them greatly.

diamond_bolt.name: diamond bolt
diamond_bolt.lore: These bolts are tipped with diamond and strike more heavily than gold. The crystal shatters as it strikes and stays in the wound, and by this ugly device a great many quarrels with armoured things have been ended.

adamantine_bolt.name: adamantine bolt
adamantine_bolt.lore: Out of adamantine, the rarest metal in the known world, the smiths forge bolts that will neither bend nor blunt. Few archers have ever found one again, yet few bolts of mortal making strike so heavily upon the hide of dragons or the plating of golems.

arrows_of_eros.name: Arrows of Eros
arrows_of_eros.lore: Eros, whom the Romans called Cupid, bore arrows of two kinds, those tipped with gold to kindle love and those tipped with lead to drive it away. Ovid tells how he shot Apollo with gold and the nymph Daphne with lead, so that the god pursued her until she was changed into a laurel tree. These arrows are of the golden kind.

arrows_of_artemis.name: Arrows of Artemis
arrows_of_artemis.unidentified_name: silver arrows fletched with white feathers
arrows_of_artemis.lore: While Artemis was yet a little girl she went to the Cyclopes upon the isle of Lipara and asked of them a bow and arrows, and with these she never missed. When a woman died suddenly and without pain, the Greeks would say, as Homer has it, that she was slain by the gentle shafts of Artemis.

bolts_of_zeus.name: Bolts of Zeus
bolts_of_zeus.lore: In thanks for their freedom the Cyclopes Brontes, Steropes and Arges forged the thunderbolt for Zeus, and with it he overthrew the Titans and established the order of Olympus. Later poets placed their forge beneath Mount Etna. Such bolts are never found in any great number, and the earth shakes at the fall of each one.

shotgun_shell.name: shotgun shell
shotgun_shell.lore: These are twelve-gauge shells of buckshot, and in each lie nine pellets of lead that spread at close range to most dreadful effect. None could mistake their red plastic hulls and bases of brass, and upon them is the brand of S-Mart.
